name: CA
title: Canada Political Compass Test 2026 | CoreOpinion
desc: Where do you stand in Canadian politics? 70 statements to see your alignment with the Liberals, Conservatives, NDP, Greens, Bloc Québécois and PPC, plus your framing bias.
keywords: Canadian political quiz, Canada political compass test, Liberal Conservative NDP quiz, where do I stand in Canadian politics, political alignment test Canada, which party should I vote for Canada, Carney Poilievre quiz, Canadian election 2025 quiz

lib.name: Liberal
lib.desc: Your answers most closely match the Liberal Party. You tend to support managed trade, social programs, climate action, and a strong federal role in the economy.

con.name: Conservative
con.desc: Your answers most closely match the Conservative Party. You favour lower taxes, smaller government, axing the carbon tax, and reducing federal spending.

ndp.name: NDP
ndp.desc: Your answers most closely match the NDP. You support pharmacare, dental care, workers rights, wealth taxes, and a more activist government on inequality and climate.

grn.name: Green
grn.desc: Your answers most closely match the Green Party. You prioritise strong climate action, proportional representation, and a systemic challenge to corporate power.

blq.name: Bloc Québécois
blq.desc: Your answers most closely match the Bloc. You support Quebec autonomy, French language protection, and a centre-left social model on federal matters.

ppc.name: PPC
ppc.desc: Your answers most closely match the PPC. You want radical cuts to immigration, elimination of climate policy, and a rejection of mainstream conservative incrementalism.

bank.q: Canada’s public healthcare must stay universal, and private, pay-for-service care should be resisted.
bank.ctx: Canada's healthcare (Medicare) is publicly funded and universal. This wants it kept that way, resisting private pay-for-service care.

bank.q: Public monopoly means endless wait times; more private options would get Canadians treated faster.
bank.ctx: This argues the public system's long wait times could be eased by allowing more private healthcare options.

bank.q: Immigration levels have been far too high and are straining housing and services.
bank.ctx: This argues Canada's recent high immigration levels have strained housing and public services and should be cut.

bank.q: Immigration built Canada and remains essential to its economy and future.
bank.ctx: This is the pro-immigration view: that immigration built Canada and remains essential to its economy and future.

bank.q: Canada should sharply cut the number of temporary foreign workers and international students.
bank.ctx: This targets the sharp rise in temporary foreign workers and international students, calling for their numbers to be cut sharply.

bank.q: Temporary workers and students fill real gaps and enrich Canada; scapegoating them is wrong.
bank.ctx: This argues those workers and students fill real gaps and enrich Canada, and shouldn't be blamed for wider problems.

bank.q: The federal carbon tax is a fair, effective way to fight climate change and should stay.
bank.ctx: The federal carbon tax charges for burning fossil fuels to fight climate change, with rebates to households. This defends it as fair and effective.

bank.q: The carbon tax is a cash grab that punishes ordinary families and should be axed.
bank.ctx: This attacks the carbon tax as a money grab that raises costs for ordinary families, and wants it scrapped ('axe the tax').

bank.q: Canada should keep expanding oil and gas production and build more pipelines.
bank.ctx: This supports expanding Canada's oil and gas industry and building more pipelines to carry it.

bank.q: Canada must wind down fossil fuel expansion and leave more oil in the ground.
bank.ctx: This argues Canada must wind down fossil-fuel expansion and leave more oil in the ground for the climate.

bank.q: Governments should build housing directly and intervene hard to bring prices down.
bank.ctx: This supports governments building housing directly and intervening strongly to bring down home prices.

bank.q: The housing crisis will be fixed by cutting red tape and letting the market build, not by government.
bank.ctx: This argues the housing crisis is best fixed by cutting red tape and letting the private market build, not by government.

bank.q: The wealthiest Canadians and big corporations should pay significantly more tax.
bank.ctx: This supports significantly higher taxes on Canada's wealthiest people and big corporations.

bank.q: Higher taxes on wealth and business just drive investment and talent out of Canada.
bank.ctx: This argues higher taxes on wealth and business drive investment and skilled people out of Canada.

bank.q: National dental care and pharmacare should be expanded, even at high cost.
bank.ctx: This supports expanding new national programs like public dental care and pharmacare (covering prescription drugs), even at high cost.

bank.q: Costly new national programs Canada can’t afford will just balloon the deficit.
bank.ctx: This argues Canada can't afford costly new national programs and they would balloon the deficit.

bank.q: Quebec should become an independent country.
bank.ctx: This supports Quebec, the mainly French-speaking province, becoming an independent country.

bank.q: Quebec is stronger within Canada, and separation would be an economic and social mistake.
bank.ctx: This opposes Quebec independence, arguing the province is stronger within Canada.

bank.q: Quebec’s law banning public servants from wearing religious symbols (Bill 21) is legitimate.
bank.ctx: Quebec's Bill 21 bans some public workers (teachers, police) from wearing religious symbols like hijabs or turbans. This defends it as legitimate secularism.

bank.q: Bill 21 is state discrimination that punishes religious minorities for how they dress.
bank.ctx: This condemns Bill 21 as state discrimination that punishes religious minorities for how they dress.

bank.q: Reconciliation with Indigenous peoples requires major new spending and returning control over land.
bank.ctx: 'Reconciliation' means repairing Canada's relationship with Indigenous peoples after historical wrongs. This supports major new spending and returning control over land.

bank.q: Reconciliation has become an endless money pit, and Canadians deserve a firm line on cost.
bank.ctx: This argues reconciliation spending has become an open-ended cost and that Canadians deserve firm limits.

bank.q: Canada should keep tightening gun control, including bans on assault-style firearms.
bank.ctx: This supports tighter gun control, including bans on assault-style firearms.

bank.q: Gun bans punish law-abiding hunters and sport shooters while doing nothing about criminals.
bank.ctx: This argues gun bans punish law-abiding hunters and sport shooters while doing nothing to stop criminals.

bank.q: Canada must stand up to the United States and retaliate against its tariffs, whatever the cost.
bank.ctx: This supports Canada standing up to the United States and retaliating against US tariffs (import taxes), whatever the cost.

bank.q: Picking fights with the US is reckless; Canada’s economy depends on getting along with its biggest partner.
bank.ctx: This argues confronting the US is reckless because Canada's economy depends on trade with its huge neighbour.

bank.q: Canada should sharply raise military spending to meet its NATO commitments.
bank.ctx: This supports sharply higher military spending to meet Canada's NATO commitments (the Western defence alliance).

bank.q: Pouring billions into the military is money better spent on Canadians at home.
bank.ctx: This argues the billions for the military would be better spent on Canadians at home.

bank.q: Safe-supply and decriminalisation are the right, evidence-based response to the drug crisis.
bank.ctx: 'Safe supply' gives drug users regulated drugs, and decriminalisation removes criminal penalties for possession. This backs both as evidence-based responses to the drug crisis.

bank.q: Safe-supply experiments flooded communities with drugs and disorder, and should be scrapped.
bank.ctx: This argues these experiments flooded communities with drugs and disorder and should be scrapped.

bank.q: Multiculturalism has failed and produced divided communities with little in common.
bank.ctx: This argues multiculturalism has failed, producing divided communities with little in common.

bank.q: Canada’s multiculturalism is a genuine strength and part of its national identity.
bank.ctx: This celebrates multiculturalism as a genuine strength and a core part of Canadian identity.

bank.q: Islam is not compatible with Canadian values.
bank.ctx: This argues Islam clashes with Canadian values. Supporters cite integration concerns; critics call it religious prejudice.

bank.q: Muslim Canadians are full members of society, and their faith deserves equal respect.
bank.ctx: This holds that Muslim Canadians are full members of society whose faith deserves equal respect.

bank.q: Some races are simply more intelligent or capable than others.
bank.ctx: This is a statement of racial supremacism — the belief that some races are inherently more intelligent or capable than others. Mainstream science rejects it, and it is historically tied to ideologies like Nazism and systems like apartheid.

bank.q: There is no hierarchy of races; the idea is pseudo-science with a shameful history.
bank.ctx: This is the principle of human equality: that no race is inherently smarter or more capable, and that the idea of a racial hierarchy is discredited pseudo-science with a shameful history.

bank.q: Sentences are too soft; violent and repeat offenders should spend far longer in prison.
bank.ctx: This argues sentences are too soft and that violent and repeat offenders should spend far longer in prison.

bank.q: Locking more people up has never made Canada safer; prevention and rehabilitation do.
bank.ctx: This argues locking more people up hasn't made Canada safer, and that prevention and rehabilitation work better.

bank.q: Trans people should be able to change their legal gender based on self-identification.
bank.ctx: This supports transgender rights: the view that people should be able to have the law recognise the gender they identify as, without needing medical approval.

bank.q: Biological sex is a reality that the law should not let a declaration override.
bank.ctx: This is the gender-critical view: that biological sex is a fixed fact the law should not allow a personal declaration to override.

bank.q: Parents should have more say over what their children are taught about gender and sexuality.
bank.ctx: This argues parents should have more say over what schools teach their children about gender and sexuality.

bank.q: Curriculum should be set by educators and evidence, not by parental veto over inclusion.
bank.ctx: This argues the curriculum should be set by educators and evidence, not by a parental veto over inclusive teaching.

bank.q: Access to abortion is a settled right and should be fully protected.
bank.ctx: This treats access to abortion as a settled right that should be fully protected. Canada has no specific abortion law.

bank.q: Abortion ends a human life, and Canada is wrong to have no legal limits at all.
bank.ctx: This argues it is wrong that Canada has no legal limits on abortion at all, and that a human life is at stake.

bank.q: Medical assistance in dying (MAID) is a compassionate right and its access is broadly appropriate.
bank.ctx: MAID (Medical Assistance in Dying) is Canada's legal assisted-death system. This defends it as compassionate and broadly appropriate.

bank.q: MAID has expanded dangerously far and now pressures the poor and disabled toward death.
bank.ctx: This argues MAID has expanded too far and now risks pushing poor or disabled people toward death.

bank.q: Workers need stronger unions and rights, and the right to strike should be protected.
bank.ctx: This supports stronger trade unions and worker rights, and protecting the right to strike.

bank.q: Union power drives up costs and holds the economy hostage; strike laws should be tightened.
bank.ctx: This argues union power raises costs and can hold the economy hostage, and that strike laws should be tightened.

bank.q: Canada over-regulates its economy; business needs far less red tape and lower taxes.
bank.ctx: This argues Canada over-regulates its economy and that business needs far less red tape and lower taxes.

bank.q: Cutting regulation just lets corporations off the hook on workers and the environment.
bank.ctx: This argues cutting regulation just lets corporations off the hook on workers and the environment.

bank.q: Canada should cut ties with the British monarchy and have its own head of state.
bank.ctx: This supports Canada cutting ties with the British monarchy (King Charles is Canada's head of state) and choosing its own.

bank.q: The Crown is part of Canada’s constitutional stability and should be kept.
bank.ctx: This defends the Crown as part of Canada's constitutional stability.

bank.q: Protecting the French language in Quebec justifies strong restrictions on English.
bank.ctx: Quebec limits the use of English to protect French. This argues that protecting French justifies strong restrictions on English.

bank.q: Language laws that restrict English go too far and trample individual freedom.
bank.ctx: This argues language laws restricting English go too far and trample individual freedom.

bank.q: Canada should replace first-past-the-post with proportional representation.
bank.ctx: This supports replacing 'first-past-the-post' (most votes wins each seat) with proportional representation, which matches seats to vote share.

bank.q: First-past-the-post gives Canada stable, accountable governments and should be kept.
bank.ctx: This defends first-past-the-post as producing stable, accountable governments.

bank.q: Open global free trade has made Canada richer and should be defended.
bank.ctx: This supports open global free trade as having made Canada richer.

bank.q: Free trade hollowed out Canadian manufacturing and left communities behind.
bank.ctx: This argues free trade hollowed out Canadian manufacturing and left communities behind.

bank.q: Protecting nature should take priority over new resource projects and development.
bank.ctx: This puts protecting nature ahead of new resource projects (mines, pipelines) and development.

bank.q: Endless environmental reviews are strangling the projects Canada needs to prosper.
bank.ctx: This argues endless environmental reviews block the projects Canada needs to prosper.

bank.q: Immigrants who won’t integrate or adopt Canadian values should not be here.
bank.ctx: This argues immigrants who won't integrate or adopt Canadian values should not be in the country.

bank.q: Demanding cultural conformity betrays the pluralism that defines Canada.
bank.ctx: This argues demanding cultural conformity betrays the pluralism (acceptance of many cultures) that defines Canada.

bank.q: Children should be taught pride in Canada’s history, not mainly its wrongs.
bank.ctx: This favours teaching children pride in Canada's history rather than focusing mainly on its wrongs.

bank.q: A country that hides its historical wrongs, like residential schools, from students is lying to them.
bank.ctx: This supports teaching hard truths like the residential schools (where Indigenous children were abused), arguing hiding them misleads students.

bank.q: The unemployed and poor are treated with too much suspicion; the safety net should be stronger.
bank.ctx: This argues the poor and unemployed are treated with too much suspicion and that the safety net should be stronger.

bank.q: Welfare too easily becomes a trap, and stricter conditions protect taxpayers who fund it.
bank.ctx: This argues welfare can trap people, and that stricter conditions protect the taxpayers who fund it.

bank.q: Long-standing traditions carry the wisdom of generations and should not be discarded lightly.
bank.ctx: This is the conservative view of tradition: that long-standing customs and institutions hold accumulated wisdom, so we should be cautious about sweeping them away for something new.

bank.q: Worshipping tradition just lets the dead govern the living and blocks necessary change.
bank.ctx: This is the progressive reply: that clinging to tradition for its own sake lets the past dictate to the present and blocks change that is needed.

bank.q: A good society depends more on personal responsibility than on government support.
bank.ctx: This reflects a right-leaning value: that a good society rests mainly on individuals taking responsibility for their own lives, rather than leaning on government.

bank.q: Blaming individuals for problems the system creates is how the comfortable excuse others’ suffering.
bank.ctx: This reflects a left-leaning value: that many problems are caused by unfair systems, so blaming individuals lets the comfortable look past suffering they may benefit from.

heroTitle: Where do you stand in Canadian politics?
heroSub: 70 statements on the issues defining Canada right now: healthcare, immigration, the carbon tax, housing, and Quebec. Every position is asked twice with opposite framing, revealing both your party alignment and your framing bias.
